candidate_relations.reason: Cockayne–Touraine DDEB is a related COL7A1 disease but not the pretibial intensely pruritic milia-rich pruriginosa phenotype.
Porphyria cutanea tarda typically affects sun-exposed dorsal hands with biochemical porphyrins, not a heterozygous COL7A1 shin-limited eruption.
Lichen simplex chronicus can mimic itchy plaques but does not produce dermoepidermal separation, milia, and a COL7A1 variant.
Dermatitis does not explain COL7A1 p.Gly2278Trp, milia, and histopathologic dermoepidermal cleavage.
Genodermatosis is the parent class of epidermolysis bullosa pruriginosa and lacks that specificity.
Dermatitis herpetiformis is a granular-IgA gluten-associated bullous disease, not a COL7A1 dystrophic EB variant.
COL7A1 mutation is the molecular finding and does not name epidermolysis bullosa pruriginosa.
Epidermolysis bullosa simplex is a keratin-gene intraepidermal disease, conflicting with COL7A1 and dermoepidermal separation.
Hallopeau–Siemens (severe recessive DEB) is generalized severe RDEB, incompatible with a heterozygous missense and isolated pretibial disease.
Hyperkeratosis/lichenification is a secondary surface change of chronic scratching, not the EB diagnosis.
Lichen sclerosus does not produce COL7A1 cleavage and milia confined to one shin for a decade.
Dominant dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa is the genetic parent of the pruriginosa subtype and omits that specifier.
Psoriasis would not show dermoepidermal separation, milia, or a pathogenic COL7A1 variant.
Dystrophic EB inversa involves flexures and mucosa; this disease is unilateral pretibial pruriginosa without mucosal lesions.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: intertriginous inversa RDEB vs pretibial EBP

candidate_relations.reason: Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa pruriginosa is the same COL7A1-related pretibial pruritic milia-rich entity as EBP.
Pruritic dermatitis describes the itch without the genetic mechanobullous diagnosis.
